lines.text: Calcutta, eighteen eighty-one. A college student named Narendranath is reading Kant.
lines.ph: kælkˈʌɾə, ˈeɪtiːn ˈeɪɾiwˌʌn. ɐ kˈɑːlɪdʒ stˈuːdənt nˈeɪmd nəɹˈeɪndɹənɑːt ɪz ɹˈiːdɪŋ kˈɑːnt.

lines.text: Kant tells him something unsettling: reason cannot see past its own walls.
lines.ph: kˈɑːnt tˈɛlz hˌɪm sˈʌmθɪŋ ʌnsˈɛɾəlɪŋ: ɹˈiːzən kænˈɑːt sˈiː pˈæst ɪts ˈoʊn wˈɔːlz.

lines.text: Years later, as Swami Vivekananda, he would say the sages of India had found that wall long before.
lines.ph: jˈɪɹz lˈeɪɾɚ, æz swˈɑːmi vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə, hiː wʊd sˈeɪ ðə sˈeɪdʒᵻz ʌv ˈɪndiə hæd fˈaʊnd ðæt wˈɔːl lˈɔŋ bᵻfˈoːɹ.

lines.text: And they had looked for a way through it.
lines.ph: ænd ðeɪ hæd lˈʊkt fɚɹə wˈeɪ θɹˈuː ɪt.

lines.text: The soul, he said, is always looking for something that does not change.
lines.ph: ðə sˈoʊl, hiː sˈɛd, ɪz ˈɔːlweɪz lˈʊkɪŋ fɔːɹ sˈʌmθɪŋ ðæt dʌznˌɑːt tʃˈeɪndʒ.

lines.text: Wealth comes and goes. Ambition is fed, and is hungry again.
lines.ph: wˈɛlθ kˈʌmz ænd ɡˈoʊz. æmbˈɪʃən ɪz fˈɛd, ænd ɪz hˈʌŋɡɹi ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: Everything we can grasp rises and falls, like a wave.
lines.ph: ˈɛvɹɪθˌɪŋ wiː kæn ɡɹˈæsp ɹˈaɪzᵻz ænd fˈɔːlz, lˈaɪk ɐ wˈeɪv.

lines.text: Religion, for him, was the search for what lies beneath the waves.
lines.ph: ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən, fɔːɹ hˈɪm, wʌzðə sˈɜːtʃ fɔːɹ wʌt lˈaɪz bᵻnˌiːθ ðə wˈeɪvz.

lines.text: Here is the discovery he credited to Kant.
lines.ph: hˈɪɹ ɪz ðə dɪskˈʌvɚɹi hiː kɹˈɛdɪɾᵻd tuː kˈɑːnt.

lines.text: Time, space and causation are not things out there. They are modes of thought.
lines.ph: tˈaɪm, spˈeɪs ænd kɔːsˈeɪʃən ɑːɹ nˌɑːt θˈɪŋz ˈaʊt ðˈɛɹ. ðeɪ ɑːɹ mˈoʊdz ʌv θˈɔːt.

lines.text: Every picture the mind makes is projected through these three.
lines.ph: ˈɛvɹi pˈɪktʃɚ ðə mˈaɪnd mˌeɪks ɪz pɹədʒˈɛktᵻd θɹuː ðiːz θɹˈiː.

lines.text: Vedanta, he said, taught this ages ago, and called it Maya.
lines.ph: veɪdˈɑːntə, hiː sˈɛd, tˈɔːt ðɪs ˈeɪdʒᵻz ɐɡˈoʊ, ænd kˈɔːld ɪt mˈɑːjɑː.

lines.text: Not a product of thought, but the groundwork of all human thought.
lines.ph: nˌɑːɾə pɹˈɑːdʌkt ʌv θˈɔːt, bˌʌt ðə ɡɹˈaʊndwɜːk ʌv ˈɔːl hjˈuːmən θˈɔːt.

lines.text: Look at a wall. Light reaches the eye, but you do not see the wall until the mind reacts.
lines.ph: lˈʊk æɾə wˈɔːl. lˈaɪt ɹˈiːtʃᵻz ðɪ ˈaɪ, bˌʌt juː duːnˌɑːt sˈiː ðə wˈɔːl ʌntˈɪl ðə mˈaɪnd ɹɪˈækts.

lines.text: Try it here. No triangle has been drawn on this card.
lines.ph: tɹˈaɪ ɪt hˈɪɹ. nˈoʊ tɹˈaɪæŋɡəl hˈæzbiːn dɹˈɔːn ˌɔn ðɪs kˈɑːɹd.

lines.text: Your mind supplies every edge.
lines.ph: jʊɹ mˈaɪnd səplˈaɪz ˈɛvɹi ˈɛdʒ.

lines.text: So the world we see is the real world, call it X, plus mind.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ ðə wˈɜːld wiː sˈiː ɪz ðə ɹˈiːəl wˈɜːld, kˈɔːl ɪɾ ˈɛks, plˈʌs mˈaɪnd.

lines.text: A blind man knows the world by touch and sound. Give us an electric sense, and the world would change again.
lines.ph: ɐ blˈaɪnd mˈæn nˈoʊz ðə wˈɜːld baɪ tˈʌtʃ ænd sˈaʊnd. ɡˈɪv ˌʌs ɐn ᵻlˈɛktɹɪk sˈɛns, ænd ðə wˈɜːld wʊd tʃˈeɪndʒ ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: Each mind brings its own world. X remains unchanged.
lines.ph: ˈiːtʃ mˈaɪnd bɹˈɪŋz ɪts ˈoʊn wˈɜːld. ˈɛks ɹᵻmˈeɪnz ʌntʃˈeɪndʒd.

lines.text: Now turn inward. The self we feel is also seen through the mind.
lines.ph: nˈaʊ tˈɜːn ˈɪnwɚd. ðə sˈɛlf wiː fˈiːl ɪz ˈɔːlsoʊ sˈiːn θɹuː ðə mˈaɪnd.

lines.text: Call the real self Y. What we know is Y plus mind.
lines.ph: kˈɔːl ðə ɹˈiːəl sˈɛlf wˈaɪ. wˌʌt wiː nˈoʊ ɪz wˈaɪ plˈʌs mˈaɪnd.

lines.text: Kant, he said, was the first to arrive at this analysis of mind. The Vedas had stated it long ago.
lines.ph: kˈɑːnt, hiː sˈɛd, wʌzðə fˈɜːst tʊ ɚɹˈaɪv æt ðɪs ɐnˈæləsˌɪs ʌv mˈaɪnd. ðˈə vˈeɪdəz hæd stˈeɪɾᵻd ɪt lˈɔŋ ɐɡˈoʊ.

lines.text: But X and Y are both beyond time, and time is what makes difference.
lines.ph: bˌʌt ˈɛks ænd wˈaɪ ɑːɹ bˈoʊθ bᵻjˌɔnd tˈaɪm, ænd tˈaɪm ɪz wʌt mˌeɪks dˈɪfɹəns.

lines.text: So they must be one. Seen outside, we call it the world. Seen inside, the Self.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ ðeɪ mˈʌst biː wˌʌn. sˈiːn aʊtsˈaɪd, wiː kˈɔːl ɪt ðə wˈɜːld. sˈiːn ɪnsˈaɪd, ðə sˈɛlf.

lines.text: Then are there two worlds, a real one hidden behind a false one?
lines.ph: ðˈɛn ɑːɹ ðɛɹ tˈuː wˈɜːldz, ɐ ɹˈiːəl wˈʌn hˈɪdən bᵻhˌaɪnd ɐ fˈɔls wˌʌn?

lines.text: No. At dusk, a man sees a snake on the path.
lines.ph: nˈoʊ. æt dˈʌsk, ɐ mˈæn sˈiːz ɐ snˈeɪk ɔnðə pˈæθ.

lines.text: Someone brings a lamp. It was a rope.
lines.ph: sˈʌmwʌn bɹˈɪŋz ɐ lˈæmp. ɪt wʌzɐ ɹˈoʊp.

lines.text: He never saw both. Seen through the senses, the world is phenomenal. It was the real all along.
lines.ph: hiː nˈɛvɚ sˈɔː bˈoʊθ. sˈiːn θɹuː ðə sˈɛnsᵻz, ðə wˈɜːld ɪz fɪnˈɑːmɪnəl. ɪt wʌzðə ɹˈiːəl ˈɔːl ɐlˈɔŋ.

lines.text: Schopenhauer said the world is will.
lines.ph: ʃˈoʊpənhaʊɚ sˈɛd ðə wˈɜːld ɪz wˈɪl.

lines.text: Vivekananda disagreed. Will needs a stimulus from outside. It is a compound, as much as a wall is.
lines.ph: vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə dˌɪsɐɡɹˈiːd. wɪl nˈiːdz ɐ stˈɪmjʊləs fɹʌm aʊtsˈaɪd. ɪɾ ɪz ɐ kˈɑːmpaʊnd, æz mˈʌtʃ æz ɐ wˈɔːl ɪz.

lines.text: And take Kant's analysis: one cannot will without willing in time.
lines.ph: ænd tˈeɪk kˈɑːnts ɐnˈæləsˌɪs: wˈʌn kænˈɑːt wɪl wɪðˌaʊt wˈɪlɪŋ ɪn tˈaɪm.

lines.text: Whatever lives inside time cannot be the Absolute.
lines.ph: wʌtˈɛvɚ lˈaɪvz ɪnsˈaɪd tˈaɪm kænˈɑːt biː ðɪ ˈæbsəlˌuːt.

lines.text: My reality, nature's, and God's, he said, are the same. Only the form differs.
lines.ph: maɪ ɹɪˈælᵻɾi, nˈeɪtʃɚz, ænd ɡˈɑːdz, hiː sˈɛd, ɑːɹ ðə sˈeɪm. ˈoʊnli ðə fˈɔːɹm dˈɪfɚz.

lines.text: The shore shapes the ocean into a bay, a strait, an inlet.
lines.ph: ðə ʃˈoːɹ ʃˈeɪps ðɪ ˈoʊʃən ˌɪntʊ ɐ bˈeɪ, ɐ stɹˈeɪt, ɐn ˈɪnlɪt.

lines.text: Take away the shaping force, and all is ocean again.
lines.ph: tˈeɪk ɐwˈeɪ ðə ʃˈeɪpɪŋ fˈoːɹs, ænd ˈɔːl ɪz ˈoʊʃən ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: Kant, he said, proved beyond doubt that we cannot get past the tremendous dead wall called reason.
lines.ph: kˈɑːnt, hiː sˈɛd, pɹˈuːvd bᵻjˌɔnd dˈaʊt ðæt wiː kænˈɑːt ɡɛt pˈæst ðə tɹəmˈɛndəs dˈɛd wˈɔːl kˈɔːld ɹˈiːzən.

lines.text: That is exactly where Indian thought takes its stand.
lines.ph: ðæt ɪz ɛɡzˈæktli wˌɛɹ ˈɪndiən θˈɔːt tˈeɪks ɪts stˈænd.

lines.text: The sages asked nature: do you know what the soul is? Nature answered, no.
lines.ph: ðə sˈeɪdʒᵻz ˈæskt nˈeɪtʃɚ: dˈuː juː nˈoʊ wʌt ðə sˈoʊl ɪz? nˈeɪtʃɚɹ ˈænsɚd, nˈoʊ.

lines.text: So they turned inward, and struck out everything that could be seen. Neti, neti. Not this, not this.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ ðeɪ tˈɜːnd ˈɪnwɚd, ænd stɹˈʌk ˈaʊt ˈɛvɹɪθˌɪŋ ðæt kʊd biː sˈiːn. nˈeɪti, nˈeɪti. nˌɑːt ðˈɪs, nˌɑːt ðˈɪs.

lines.text: When every appearance has been negated, whatever remains, that is It.
lines.ph: wˌɛn ˈɛvɹi ɐpˈɪɹəns hˈæzbiːn nᵻɡˈeɪɾᵻd, wʌtˈɛvɚ ɹᵻmˈeɪnz, ðˈæt ɪz ɪt.

lines.text: Is what lies beyond thought only the dull silence of a stone?
lines.ph: ɪz wʌt lˈaɪz bᵻjˌɔnd θˈɔːt ˈoʊnli ðə dˈʌl sˈaɪləns əvə stˈoʊn?

lines.text: Light vibrating too slowly, we cannot see. Faster, it becomes light. Faster still, it is dark to us again.
lines.ph: lˈaɪt vˈaɪbɹeɪɾɪŋ tˈuː slˈoʊli, wiː kænˈɑːt sˈiː. fˈæstɚ, ɪt bɪkˌʌmz lˈaɪt. fˈæstɚ stˈɪl, ɪɾ ɪz dˈɑːɹk tʊ ˌʌs ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: The two darknesses are as different as the two poles.
lines.ph: ðə tˈuː dˈɑːɹknəsᵻz ɑːɹ æz dˈɪfɹənt æz ðə tˈuː pˈoʊlz.

lines.text: The stone cannot reason. God does not need to.
lines.ph: ðə stˈoʊn kænˈɑːt ɹˈiːzən. ɡˈɑːd dʌznˌɑːt nˈiːd tuː.

lines.text: Was this Kant's idea, carried East? Vivekananda said it was the other way round.
lines.ph: wʌz ðˈɪs kˈɑːnts aɪdˈiə, kˈæɹid ˈiːst? vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə sˈɛd ɪt wʌzðɪ ˈʌðɚ wˈeɪ ɹˈaʊnd.

lines.text: Shankara had identified time, space and causation with Maya, many centuries before.
lines.ph: ʃˈʌŋkəɹə hæd aɪdˈɛntᵻfˌaɪd tˈaɪm, spˈeɪs ænd kɔːsˈeɪʃən wɪð mˈɑːjɑː, mˈɛni sˈɛntʃɚɹiz bᵻfˈoːɹ.

lines.text: He found the passages in Shankara's commentaries, and sent them to his friend, Professor Max Muller.
lines.ph: hiː fˈaʊnd ðə pˈæsɪdʒᵻz ˈɪn ʃˈʌŋkəɹəz kˈɑːməntˌɛɹiz, ænd sˈɛnt ðˌɛm tə hɪz fɹˈɛnd, pɹəfˈɛsɚ mˈæks mˈʊlɚ.

lines.text: Is the world unreal, then? A devotee once asked Ramakrishna.
lines.ph: ɪz ðə wˈɜːld ʌnɹˈiːəl, ðˈɛn? ɐ dˌɛvoʊtˈiː wˈʌns ˈæskt ɹˌɑːməkɹˈɪʃnə.

lines.text: While you climb, he said, you reason: the stairs are not the roof. Not this, not this.
lines.ph: wˌaɪl juː klˈaɪm, hiː sˈɛd, juː ɹˈiːzən: ðə stˈɛɹz ɑːɹ nˌɑːt ðə ɹˈuːf. nˌɑːt ðˈɪs, nˌɑːt ðˈɪs.

lines.text: Reach the roof, and you see the stairs are made of the same brick and lime.
lines.ph: ɹˈiːtʃ ðə ɹˈuːf, ænd juː sˈiː ðə stˈɛɹz ɑːɹ mˌeɪd ʌvðə sˈeɪm bɹˈɪk ænd lˈaɪm.

lines.text: God himself has become the universe. But reasoning alone will not show it.
lines.ph: ɡˈɑːd hɪmsˈɛlf hɐz bɪkˌʌm ðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs. bˌʌt ɹˈiːzənɪŋ ɐlˈoʊn wɪl nˌɑːt ʃˈoʊ ɪt.

lines.text: Kant drew the wall. The Upanishads asked who stands behind it.
lines.ph: kˈɑːnt dɹˈuː ðə wˈɔːl. ðˈə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz ˈæskt hˌuː stˈændz bᵻhˈaɪnd ɪt.

lines.text: If we are bound, Vivekananda asked, who bound us? No power can bind the Infinite but Itself.
lines.ph: ɪf wiː ɑːɹ bˈaʊnd, vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə ˈæskt, hˌuː bˈaʊnd ˌʌs? nˈoʊ pˈaʊɚ kæn bˈaɪnd ðɪ ˈɪnfɪnət bˌʌt ɪtsˈɛlf.

lines.text: Which came first, the bird or the egg? Give it up. Escape from Maya.
lines.ph: wˌɪtʃ kˈeɪm fˈɜːst, ðə bˈɜːd ɔːɹ ðɪ ˈɛɡ? ɡˈɪv ɪɾ ˈʌp. ɛskˈeɪp fɹʌm mˈɑːjɑː.

lines.text: And the student who studied Kant went looking for a man who had seen beyond the wall.
lines.ph: ænd ðə stˈuːdənt hˌuː stˈʌdid kˈɑːnt wɛnt lˈʊkɪŋ fɚɹə mˈæn hˌuː hæd sˈiːn bᵻjˌɔnd ðə wˈɔːl.
